content.user_title: Build UMAP Embeddings for Data Analysis
content.value_statement: High-dimensional data can be hard to visualize, cluster, and reuse in machine learning workflows. This skill guides UMAP setup, tuning, supervised use, and advanced variants.
actual_capabilities: Explain when to use UMAP for visualization, clustering preprocessing, or feature engineering.
Recommend core parameters such as n_neighbors, min_dist, n_components, metric, and random_state.
Outline supervised and semi-supervised UMAP workflows with label guidance.
Describe transform, inverse_transform, Parametric UMAP, DensMAP, and AlignedUMAP use.
Provide troubleshooting guidance for fragmented clusters, slow runs, and collapsed embeddings.
limitations: The skill provides guidance; execution depends on available Python packages and data access.
UMAP embeddings can vary between runs unless random_state and preprocessing are controlled.
Clustering results still need external validation because UMAP can create artificial separations.
Parametric UMAP guidance assumes TensorFlow and compatible hardware are available.

use_cases.title: Tune Embeddings for Visualization
use_cases.description: Choose preprocessing, metrics, and parameters that make high-dimensional data easier to inspect in two or three dimensions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Features for Models
use_cases.description: Use UMAP transformations as compact features for downstream classifiers or reusable machine learning pipelines.

use_cases.title: Compare Related Experiments
use_cases.description: Plan aligned embeddings for temporal, batch, or repeated experimental datasets while keeping coordinate systems comparable.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a UMAP Starting Point
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: I have high-dimensional [data type] with [rows] samples and [features] features. Recommend a simple UMAP setup for visualization, including preprocessing, metric choice, and starting parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Tune a UMAP Plot
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my UMAP result: [describe plot]. Suggest parameter changes for n_neighbors, min_dist, metric, and random_state to improve [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Design UMAP for Clustering
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a UMAP plus HDBSCAN workflow for [dataset]. Specify preprocessing, UMAP dimensions, clustering settings to test, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Advanced UMAP Variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Select standard, parametric, density, or aligned methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether standard UMAP, Parametric UMAP, DensMAP, or AlignedUMAP fits [workflow]. Compare tradeoffs, prerequisites, and failure modes.

output_examples.input: I need a UMAP setup for text embeddings.
output: Use cosine distance after confirming the vectors are already scaled or normalized.
Start with 15 neighbors, two output dimensions, and a fixed random state for visualization.
Increase neighbors if the map is too fragmented; validate any apparent clusters.

output_examples.input: Can I use UMAP before HDBSCAN?
output: Yes. Use more than two dimensions for clustering preprocessing when possible.
Use a tight minimum distance and test several neighborhood sizes.
Evaluate clusters with labels, stability checks, or domain review.

output_examples.input: My test embeddings look wrong after transform.
output: Check whether train and test distributions match.
Reuse the same scaler fitted on training data.
Consider Parametric UMAP if new data differs strongly or transform speed matters.

best_practices: Standardize numeric features before fitting UMAP unless the metric and data type justify another preprocessing step.
Set random_state when reproducibility matters, and record parameter values with each embedding.
Use different parameter settings for visualization, clustering preprocessing, and downstream modeling.
anti_patterns: Treating UMAP plots as proof of real clusters without validation.
Using two-dimensional embeddings as the only input for density-based clustering.
Changing preprocessing, metric, and parameters at once without tracking the effect.

faq.question: Does this skill run UMAP automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Execution depends on the host tool, Python environment, and dataset access.

faq.question: When should I choose UMAP over t-SNE?
faq.answer: Use UMAP when you need faster embeddings, transform support, or higher-dimensional outputs for machine learning workflows.

faq.question: Which metric should I start with?
faq.answer: Use euclidean for scaled numeric data, cosine for text embeddings, and hamming or jaccard for binary data.

faq.question: Can UMAP be used before clustering?
faq.answer: Yes. Use clustering-focused settings, keep more than two dimensions when possible, and validate clusters independently.

faq.question: How do I make results reproducible?
faq.answer: Set random_state, keep preprocessing fixed, and record versions and parameters.

faq.question: What is Parametric UMAP useful for?
faq.answer: It learns a neural network mapping, which can speed up transforms and support reconstruction workflows when TensorFlow is available.
